udk_analysis: Rodgers spent the majority of last offseason pondering his NFL future before landing in Pittsburgh on a one-year deal with Mike Tomlin. In classic Steelers fashion, Rodgers did enough to help them stay competitive and make the playoffs, but they ultimately fell short in the Wild Card Round. Back with the Steelers again, at this point in his career, the vet isn't really on the radar for fantasy outside of 2QB formats.

In Weeks 1-8, the magic we saw from “Laser” Mayfield in 2024 looked like it was here to stay. He was in the MVP conversation on the back of a 13:2 TD-to-INT ratio with the team eyeing the postseason. However, after the bye, Baker stumbled, throwing nine INTs while struggling to get there for fantasy. He battled through some injuries, his OL was banged up, and his pass-catchers never quite felt in sync. With Mike Evans gone, there are some question marks with the offense that now employs its fifth different play-caller in five years. Baker is another late-round QB that should only be drafted in 1QB leagues if you buy into Tampa Bay’s early season schedule.

Nix disappointed in a sophomore season where he led the NFL in pass attempts and the Broncos were the AFC's No. 1 seed. Apart from three monster games, he was relatively uninspiring as a fantasy starter, including six weeks scoring below 15 fantasy points. Despite having one of the best offensive lines in the business, he tied Shedeur Sanders and J.J. McCarthy for lowest yards per pass attempt when pressured. We still are in on Nix for fantasy with the arrival of Jaylen Waddle and an off season of recovering from his brutal ankle injury. Consider pairing him with another late-round QB as you see how he responds as a runner in the first month of the season.

After missing half the season with a toe injury, fantasy managers hopped on Purdy’s back in the fantasy playoffs as he finished the season as the QB5, 4, and 1. Always underappreciated in fantasy, his 6.2% career TD rate is the fourth best ever for a QB through their first 50 games. We always want to buy into the 49ers offense as long as CMC is alive and well; with the addition of Mike Evans, perhaps Purdy can find the formula to enter into top-10 territory at the position.

First, the good: Young led his Panthers to an NFC South title and a close loss to the Rams in the Wild Card Round of the Playoffs. He also set career-highs in completion percentage (64%), passing TDs (23), and rush attempts. Yet, he exceeded 20+ fantasy points in just three games on the season and felt impossible to get a read on week-to-week. The NFC South is a weak division, but unless we see a spike in his scramble rate and pass attempts, topping 25 passing TDs would be a small miracle. It feels tough finding routes for Young to break through as anything more than a mid-QB2 for fantasy.

Williams set the Bears’ all-time passing yardage mark (3,942), improved his pressure-to-sack ratio mightily, and had five games of 24+ fantasy points in Year 2. However, the erratic play still frustrates fantasy managers as he completed just 58% of his passes, a mark surpassing only Shedeur Sanders and J.J. McCarthy. He was more effective as a runner, including adding three scores on the ground. In Year 2 of the Ben Johnson system, perhaps there is room for Caleb to fly even higher and finish as a top-5 QB.

The Titans took Cam Ward first overall in the 2025 NFL Draft, and this is the perfect example of what can happen to a young, talented QB in their first year in the league. No disrespect to the good folks of Nashville, but this was set up to fail from the get-go as the Titans trailed on 72% of his dropbacks, fifth highest in the NFL. He tied Geno Smith for the most sacks taken (55!) and finished with just one top-12 finish on the year, albeit against Super Bowl Champion Seattle in Week 12. The addition of Wan’Dale Robinson and fourth overall pick Carnell Tate gives him a shot at a Year 2 breakout. However, unless he starts running more, Ward will likely be left amongst a pile of other QBs you could stream, but need a big spike in TD rate to matter.

The Cardinals selected Beck in the third round, making him the third QB taken in the draft. His experience (43 college starts) certainly helped his cause after the team brought him in for a top-30 visit. He can get the ball out quickly on 3step drops and hit his receivers in stride in zone coverage. His arm strength is subpar, but it should not shock anyone if Beck ends up finishing the season as the Cardinals' starting QB on a team destined for a top-5 pick. The decline is painful to watch as Stroud went from fantasy darling as a rookie in 2023 to an afterthought and liability the last two seasons. He has averaged just 218 passing yards per game with six total top-12 finishes, the same number he totaled as a rookie. With arguably the best defense in the NFL, the Texans do not need Stroud to put up gaudy numbers to compete. He is stuck in redraft purgatory as a QB likely sitting on your waiver wire to be picked up only for plus matchups.

For the first eight weeks of the season, Jones was the QB6, averaging 20.5 fantasy points per game and a scintillating 71% completion percentage. The Colts were 8-2 heading into their Week 11 bye, and then the world came crashing My Guy Sleeper Breakout Value Rookie Bust Injury Concerns Colety Crusaders Redraft Rankings 9/2/2026 down with a brutal season-ending Achilles tear. Our injury timeline suggests he will be limited throughout the off-season and could be compromised early in the 2026 season, especially as a runner.
current_alert_summary: HC Shane Steichen named Jones (signed 1yr/$14M) the unquestioned Week 1 starter over Anthony Richardson; recovering from a torn Achilles suffered Dec 7, 2025, but per a July 14, 2026 team report has taken 'nearly every first-team rep' through camp/preseason.

udk_analysis: This is a tricky situation in Cleveland. We have not seen Watson be meaningful in fantasy since (checks… rechecks) 2020! Seriously, he averaged 13.2 fantasy points per game in 18 starts over multiple years, dealing with injuries and the scrutiny of NFL fans and the media. The Browns have named Watson as their Week 1 starter, but he is nowhere near consideration for fantasy outside of deeper 2QB leagues. We expect Shedeur Sanders to make starts at some point this season.
current_alert_summary: Head coach Todd Monken named Watson the Browns' Week 1 starter (vs Jacksonville, Sept 13) over 2025 fifth-round pick / 2025 midseason starter Shedeur Sanders, based on 'whole body of work' through camp and preseason.

udk_analysis: The signs were there in Year 1 that Maye was likely going to be a good starter in this league, but what he did in Year 2 was amazing. He was barely edged out by Matthew Stafford for league MVP, but in any other season, Maye easily could have taken home that award. He led the league in EPA per play and completion percentage while finishing inside the top-five at the position in fantasy points per drop back, which is pretty insane considering his porous offensive line and a middling pass-catching group. Add A.J. Brown to the mix and we are still bullish on the young superstar. Through 28 full games in his career, he is averaging 31 rushing yards per game, which gives him a weekly floor to finish as a top-5 QB again.

Mendoza’s storybook college career is one of the most compelling parts of the No. 1 overall pick. From his humble beginnings as a lightly recruited three-star QB to transferring to Indiana and having a season for the ages, which ended in an undefeated national championship. He jumped in every single meaningful statistical category and became Indiana’s first-ever Heisman Trophy winner and the first in the Big Ten since 2006. The Raiders are starting fresh with playcaller Klint Kubiak at the helm. In Year 1, Mendoza will likely take some lumps. He is off the redraft radar, waiting his turn to start behind veteran Kirk Cousins.

You cannot make this stuff up - the Jets traded for Geno Smith, coming full circle on a player they once took in the second round of the NFL Draft way back in 2013! He was a shell of himself last year in Las Vegas, ranking dead last among all QBs in sack rate (10.6%) and INTs (17). For fantasy purposes, Geno is off the radar, but we would be satisfied if he gives Garrett Wilson 200 targets. At some point, expect the Jets to eventually replace him with fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik for a few starts as they look to 2027’s QB class.
current_alert_summary: Jets acquired Smith via trade ahead of his expected release from Las Vegas; HC Aaron Glenn stated 'We brought in Geno to be our starter,' replacing 2025 starter Justin Fields (traded to Kansas City).

udk_analysis: Where’s the Beef? Brissett was cookin’ last year for fantasy purposes, averaging over 40 pass attempts per game in his starts. His nine consecutive top-12 fantasy finishes were the most of 2025, thanks in large part to the team trailing on 73% of his dropbacks. Despite the fact that the Cardinals went 1-11 in his starts, he remains the incumbent veteran starter with Kyler Murray now donning Viking purple. He remains on the streaming radar, although we expect the passing volume to slightly decrease with new head coach Mike LaFleur calling the shots.
current_alert_summary: After Arizona released Kyler Murray, Brissett agreed to a reworked one-year deal (~$15.5M) and HC Mike LaFleur confirmed him as the likely Week 1 starter over third-round rookie Carson Beck.

udk_analysis: Are fantasy managers experiencing name fatigue? Hurts is coming off a season with the worst consistency metrics of his career, including averaging just 16.3 fantasy points per game from Week 9 on. We saw his fewest TDs inside the 5-yard line and now with AJ Brown leaving and yet another OC change, perhaps fantasy managers are scared off. While Hurts isn't a slouch as a passer, we love him in fantasy for his ability to use his legs. The overall Philly offense should return to form, making Hurts a relative value compared to where he was being drafted in the past.

Impress your friends by letting them know the only QBs to finish inside the top-10 at the position each of the last four years: Josh Allen, Jalen Hurts, and… drumroll… Jared Goff. The first half was middling with just one top-12 finish, but he responded when things mattered for fantasy, averaging 20.3 fantasy points per game from Weeks 10-16. He imploded in Week 17 at Minnesota (two INTs, three fumbles, five sacks), but that is the game you play with Goff. He offers nothing in the run game, keeping his ceiling around that QB10 mark. The Lions are favored in 14 of their first 15 games, including a juicy Week 1 matchup at home against the Saints. We know what Goff is at this point: a streaky streamer who remains one of the best at dicing up zone coverages.

After the Giants traded up in the first round to take Dart, he exceeded expectations as a rookie, averaging 41 rushing yards per game in his starts, the fifth best among rookie QBs ever. He tied Drake Maye for fourth-best in fantasy points per dropback last year despite attempting three total passes to Malik Nabers before he went down. Dart’s upside is enticing despite the fact that he plays with reckless abandon. His ADP is not accounting for a Year 2 leap, making him a prime candidate to roll with as a late-round QB.

After a storybook rookie season, the Washington Commanders nosedived in Year 2 of the Jayden Daniels era as he struggled with injuries (knee, hamstring, and elbow) before being shut down in Week 15 for the season. His rushing numbers remained on par with 2024, but the cast of receivers certainly let him down as 11% of his passes were dropped, the highest rate in the NFL. Daniels can be a difference-making fantasy asset due to his legs, but drafters are not giving any sort of discount this year. In other words, you will have to pay up for what he did as a rookie and the hope that he can return to top-5 status.

Through six seasons as Cincy’s signal-caller, Burrow has three elite fantasy seasons and three injury-plagued disappointments. In 2025, he went down in Week 2 and did not return until Week 13. Those final six weeks were vintage Burrow as he put together a 17-game pace of 4500+ passing yards and 43 passing TDs. It also helps that the Cincy defense has a ton of holes, forcing shootouts and more passing volume Burrow’s way. While we don’t love living and dying with TD rates from pocket passers, Burrow runs just enough to ignore that rule. They throw enough inside the red zone to justify his ADP.

Love's 23 passing TDs and 3300+ yards might not stand out, but efficiency has always been the name of his game. He ranked sixth in Passer Rating, seventh in completion percentage over expectation, and tied Patrick Mahomes for 12th in fantasy points per dropback. He remains one of the more polarizing starters in the league, as we have seen some really high-end play at times, yet he hasn't put it all together for a full season. For fantasy purposes, we are viewing Love as a streamer to start the season as Green Bay begins the year favored in each of their first six matchups.

He is him. While technically Allen finished with his lowest fantasy points per game average since 2019, he continued his streak of being the QB1 or QB2 for the sixth consecutive season. In 2024, Allen became the first top-5 fantasy QB without a top-36 scoring WR or top-12 TE. In 2025, he did it again. Same exact thing. Yes, he is now 30 years old, and the Bills mixed things up, firing HC Sean McDermott. The offense should remain the same, with the WR corps hopefully upgraded with the addition of DJ Moore. Allen is our unquestioned QB1 and the first pick in 2QB/SuperFlex leagues. However, in 1QB leagues, we caution taking him at the end of Round 2 and would prefer to load up on RBs or WRs.

It is a miracle Big Herbs is still alive. After losing both starting All-Pro tackles, he took a career-high number of hits and was sacked 54 times, easily the most of his career. Even with all that, he managed to bank a QB9 finish, thanks mostly to career highs in rush attempts (83) and rushing yards (498). If that part of his game can stick around and his line can stay healthy, the weapons are there for Herbert to have one of the best seasons of his career in 2026. Mike McDaniel is one of the most creative play-callers in the league, so we are bullish on Herbert if you can get him late in your drafts.

After two middling years in Atlanta, Cousins signed a “five-year” contract with Las Vegas, but only $11.3 million was guaranteed. He reunites with Klint Kubiak, who was his play-caller during his time in Minnesota. Expect Captain Kirk to potentially start the beginning of the season before giving way to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. In other words, Cousins is a first-round pick in your “QB-mentors-only” leagues but off the radar for fantasy in any other format.
current_alert_summary: New HC Klint Kubiak named Cousins (signed as FA after 2025 stint with Atlanta) the Week 1 starter (vs Miami) over rookie Fernando Mendoza, the 2026 #1 overall pick, who opens the season as backup.

udk_analysis: The Kyler Murray era in Arizona officially came to a close with the Cardinals releasing the former No. 1 overall pick in early March. Still just 28 years old, Kyler will look to get his career back on track in Minnesota, perhaps following the path of guys like Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold. Expect the team to frame this as a QB competition throughout the summer, but if you watched JJ "Nine" McCarthy play NFL football in 2025, you likely know where this is headed in terms of the Week 1 starter. We are still keeping the light on for Kyler to return to being a top-10 fantasy QB.
current_alert_summary: After being released by Arizona, Murray signed with Minnesota and was named the Week 1 starter by HC Kevin O'Connell over J.J. McCarthy, ending the competition about two weeks into camp.

udk_analysis: For the first three weeks of the season, it was vintage Lamar, averaging 27.6 fantasy points on the back of three passing TDs and 39 rushing yards per game. Unfortunately, a back injury altered his season and the future of the Baltimore Ravens. After returning in Week 9, he never quite looked like himself, averaging just 13.5 fantasy points, 1.2 passing TDs, and 20 rushing yards per game. With John Harbaugh out, it feels like a different era in Baltimore. Lamar’s raw pass attempts remain low yet continue to be the most valuable in fantasy: 40% were 10+ air yards (second highest in NFL) and 9% were “end-zone” attempts, the highest rate in the NFL. He remains in the annual top-5 QB conversation, but we would prefer if he slipped into the fourth or fifth round in redraft.

Willis' time in Tennessee was pretty forgettable, to say the least. The team took him in the third round back in 2022 and moved on after just three starts in two years. However, he landed in Green Bay as Jordan Love's backup and now has a chance to revitalize his career as a starter after getting some great coaching from Matt LaFleur. We have seen other young QBs (Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, Daniel Jones, for example) take similar paths: dumped by their original organization, sit and learn for a couple of years as a backup, and then get a second chance at a starting gig elsewhere. Could Willis be next? For fantasy, the Dolphins project to be among the worst teams in the league with straight buns at WR, but we know his mobility (41, 73, & 60 rushing yards in three starts last year) works at the QB position for the game we play. Willis certainly has the wheels to put up fantasy-friendly numbers and is worth monitoring early on in the year as a streamer.
current_alert_summary: Miami released Tua Tagovailoa and signed Willis to a 3-year, $67.5M deal same-day, naming him the 2026 starting QB and reuniting him with HC Jeff Hafley from their Packers days.

udk_analysis: It was an all-time season for the future Hall of Famer, becoming one of six QBs ever with 4700 passing yards & 46 TDs in a season. It wasn’t just stat-padding, as his nine top-6 finishes were the most among all QBs. 33 of his 46 TDs were inside the red zone, by far the most in the league. We caution going all-in on non-mobile QBs coming off a year where his TD rate went to the moon. Stafford will likely settle into low-end QB1 territory, but you have an opportunity to scoop him up as your team’s QB2 to pair with another.

The Falcons were roasted for surprisingly taking Penix eighth overall in 2024, and the results thus far are barf-worthy. In two seasons, Penix has started 12 total games while completing less than 60% of his passes. For context, that ranks 29th among 33 QBs taken in the first round of NFL Drafts over the last decade. He suffered a torn ACL in Week 11 last year, and off-season reports suggest the team is not rushing his rehab with Tua Tagovailoa now in tow as competition.
current_alert_summary: Recovering from a season-ending ACL injury (Week 11, 2025). As of Aug 31, 2026, reported to be moving into 'pole position' for the Week 1 start over Tua Tagovailoa; not yet an officially-confirmed decision by Falcons GM Ian Cunningham. Penix himself says he still has mental hurdles trusting the knee

udk_analysis: After a year in which the Chiefs failed to make the playoffs, and Mahomes tore his left ACL in Week 15, we have to reassess the aura surrounding the Kansas City QB. It is going to be really fascinating to track his recovery all offseason as he comes off the ACL plus LCL surgery. For fantasy, it is highly unlikely we will see the rushing production we saw in 2025, when Mahomes set career highs in per-game rushing attempts, yards, and TDs. The Chiefs are gifted with a “third-place” schedule and a core group willing to go for one more title run. The addition of Kenneth Walker III could take some pressure off Mahomes trying to Superman this thing every week. For fantasy purposes, he is a low-end QB1 with a name carrying more weight in your home leagues than actual fantasy-winning production.
current_alert_summary: Recovering from a torn ACL/LCL that ended his 2025 season. Has not missed a training-camp practice since being cleared in July and is reported (via NFL Network's Ian Rapoport) to be on track for Week 1, though he has not played in any 2026 preseason game and this is not yet a formal team confirmatio

udk_analysis: Oh, the tales we get to tell our grandchildren about Sam Darnold resurrecting from the fantasy grave! The Super Bowl Champion has 60(!) passing TDs over the last two seasons (tied for fifth most in the NFL) with the second-best yards per pass attempt (8.2) in that span. His passing volume declined down the stretch as Seattle came up with a winning formula, leaning on the run and a play-action-based offense that hyper-targeted Jaxon Smith-Njigba. We are happy for the man Darnold, but he still belongs only in the streaming fantasy category despite his success.

Sanders wasn’t that bad, right? Welp, after checking the numbers, we can report back that it was hot garbage ranking dead last in catchable target rate (66.5%), completion percentage (56.6%), and Passer Rating (68.1). He did have one week for fantasy (QB2 vs. TEN in Week 14) that gave you a glimpse of the upside, but there is no guarantee for him to be the long-term solution for Cleveland. The Browns named Deshaun Watson their Week 1 starter, but we do expect Sanders to eventually make a handful of starts. In that scenario, even in SuperFlex leagues, we shy away from expecting anything out of the former fifth-round pick.

Tua’s time in Miami came to a crashing end as he was cut for an NFL-record $99.2 million in dead cap money. The Falcons, scooping up every known left-handed QB in the universe, signed him for the veteran minimum ($1 million) to pair with Michael Penix Jr., who is returning from a season-ending ACL injury. Tua’s yards per attempt declined in three straight seasons (8.9 > 8.3 > 7.2 > 6.9), signaling that the former fifth overall pick’s best days are likely behind him. Nevertheless, he could begin the season as Atlanta’s starter, but is irrelevant to the fantasy conversation.
current_alert_summary: Released by Miami in March 2026, signed a 1-year/$1.2M deal with Atlanta to compete with Michael Penix Jr. As of Aug 31, 2026, reported (via ESPN's Adam Schefter) that Penix appears to be moving ahead for the Week 1 job; no final decision officially announced by Falcons management as of the report.

udk_analysis: Tyler Shough truthers, take a bow. Entering the 2025 NFL Draft cycle, a lot was made about Shough's age, but credit to New Orleans, they seem to have found a diamond in the rough. Over his final five starts, he averaged 20 fantasy points per game, a 70% completion percentage, and 27 rushing yards per game. He unlocked Chris Olave and showed out with the best completion percentage in the intermediate area of the field (11-19 yards). We believe in Kellen Moore as a play-caller, and the addition of eighth overall pick Jordyn Tyson to the WR room gives Shough another weapon at his disposal. However, Tyson is set to miss multiple regular season games after suffering a hamstring injury in camp. That does take some of the early-season excitement away from Shough, who was one of our favorite late-round targets in drafts prior to the Tyson injury.

“Uncle Jerome” had a brief moment filling in Cleveland a couple of years back, but at this point, he is nothing more than another camp body. Someone in the Washington backfield will get the short end of the stick after training camp and pre-season. Sorry, Jerome, but everyone is pointing at you.

udk_analysis: The seventh-round pick from 2025 was a trendy sleeper pick last year, as fantasy managers cited “well, Isaiah Pacheco was a seventh-round pick too!” Smith was sparingly used all season, touching the ball 79 total times despite the uninspiring play of veterans Kareem Hunt and Pacheco. With Kenneth Walker III now aboard, he is back to being a rotational back with little path forward in fantasy.

After averaging 4.9 yards per carry for the first eight seasons of his career, Aaron Jones finally hit a wall in Year 9, setting career lows in yards per carry (4.2), rushing TDs (2), and yards after contact per attempt (2.67). He remains under contract for one more year in Minnesota, sharing the backfield with Jordan Mason. The Vikings begin the season with a rough three-week stretch (GB, @ CHI, @ TB) before things open up. We have him ranked as a low-end FLEX option with unknowns at the QB and betting that the wheels finally fall off of his insanely efficient career on a per-touch basis.

Randall came to Clemson as a highly regarded WR and ended his senior year as an intriguing RB prospect after collecting 13 total TDs and 36 receptions. He was taken on Day 3, most notably as someone hand-selected by the team’s owner, which is either the best thing or the worst thing, depending on your point of view. Perhaps he can earn the RB2 role behind the Big Dog, but the most likely outcome is that he is just a role player in Year 1. Randall is beginning the season on IR because of injury.

The artist formerly known as “AJ Villain” is in Year 6 of the feature film production known as “Quadzilla”. While there was a ton of hype early on for this movie, the reviews are in: Dillon is better suited for the “hired muscle” role than as a featured final boss. He technically is on the Carolina roster, but could easily be cut come August with just $100,000 guaranteed in his contract.

From his rookie year in 2017 until 2024, only Derrick Henry scored more fantasy points than Alvin Kamara. He was truly a generational fantasy back and arguably the most dependable pass-catcher at the RB position. He hit a fantasy wall in 2025, averaging the fewest yards per carry (3.6) of his career while scoring one total TD and bowing out to an injury in Week 12. With the signing of Travis Etienne Jr., it remains to be seen what type of role he will have in this offense in 2026. You might see the name in your player pool, but remind yourself that the good ole days are gone. On top of Kamara's decline as a player, he's now dealing with a sprained MCL that is expected to sideline him for the remainder of training camp. He may miss regular season games as well depending on his recovery goes, which makes him a tough click as anything more than a late round depth option for your bench.
current_alert_summary: Sprained MCL (no tear) in an Aug 18, 2026 joint practice vs Dallas; reported out 'at least a month,' which lines up to make him likely to miss the Sept 13 opener at Detroit and puts Week 2 (at Baltimore) in question.

udk_analysis: Let’s be clear: Jeanty checks nearly every box we want in fantasy. Jeanty was actually Jason’s ‘Bust’ pick last year on the show, relative to ADP. It is not because we all didn’t love the talent and draft capital, but it is hard to be a fantasy difference maker at the RB position when your surroundings are as bad as they were a season ago. The O-line was a disaster, Pete Carroll ran a completely unserious operation, and Geno Smith regressed massively. It led to Las Vegas ranking dead last in TDs per game. Again, it is hard to be a great fantasy RB when that’s the case. Fast forward one year, and suddenly, we are more optimistic about where the Raiders are headed. Sure, Fernando Mendoza is a bit of a question mark, but the team put significant investment in the O-line, and we are big fans of Klint Kubiak’s scheme. Look for Jeanty to make a big-time jump in his efficiency metrics in Year 2, and if the Raiders offense can just be around league average, he could push for a top-8 RB season. Beyond the 29 rushing TDs last year as a Heisman runner-up, he is also one of three first-round RBs to see 20+ of their team’s receiving yardage in a single season (2023), joining some guys named Christian McCaffrey and Jahmyr Gibbs. The Raiders certainly were smitten, taking him higher than any RB in the NFL draft since Saquon Barkley in 2018. If you possess this type of draft capital (sixth overall) and elite college production at this young of an age (21 years old), you crush for fantasy. Expect a mammoth workload on a much-improved Raiders team. Fantasy drafters do, however, need to track his health closely ahead of Week 1 after he exited practice early on 8/23 with an ankle injury. The recovery timeline has not been reported, but most believe this is not a long-term injury. It's possible he's limited to begin the regular season.
current_alert_summary: Sprained his ankle diving for a pass at practice; as of the Raiders' final roster cutdown had not been cleared to practice. Team said it has 'another week to assess' before the Sept 13 opener vs Miami; not placed on IR. Backup Mike Washington Jr. is the contingency.

udk_analysis: After spending his rookie year in Denver, the one known as “Estime Lauder” found his way on the Saints roster and willed his way to two top-15 finishes in the final two weeks of the season. Before you get too excited, realize the entire Saints backfield depth chart was on injured reserve. Free agent signing Travis Etienne Jr. will be the bell-cow while Estimé occasionally mixes in for a handful of carries. Despite playing behind Travis Etienne Jr., the fourth-round pick finished fifth in rush success rate and 11th in forced missed tackle rate among 55 qualifying RBs. He was also much better inside the 10-yard line than Etienne, converting his eight rush attempts into five scores compared to 26 and only four. He profiled as a tackle-breaker coming out of college and now has a chance to be the lead back on an offense we like after Travis Etienne signed in New Orleans. We can see him return RB2 fantasy value on an offense we want pieces from for our rosters.

It was a video game-like 2025 season for Bijan, totaling 2,298 yards from scrimmage, the most since CMC in 2019. He accounted for 41% of Atlanta’s total team yardage thanks to ranking first among all RBs in forced missed tackles and percentage of the team’s first-read targets. If you are splitting hairs at the top of your drafts, the only knock on Bijan might be the functionality of the Atlanta offense and how the QB position shakes out. He is all that is great in fantasy football and a true building block if you have the pleasure of drafting him.

The Rams finally did it. They lessened the workload on Kyren Williams in 2025 after hinting at it for a couple of seasons. In 2024, when Corum was a rookie, he wasn’t a factor at all. However, in his sophomore campaign, he siphoned off 159 total opportunities for a 35% share of the carries. Kyren is obviously the lead back in this offense, but it is entirely possible Corum pushes that number closer to the 40 - 45% mark. If he does, he could have standalone value as a weekly FLEX play. Of course, should Kyren go down, Corum would project as a no-brainer weekly RB1, so he is also one of fantasy’s most valuable insurance policies while playing for one of the best offenses in the league.

Honest question: Do you have any memory of Allen contributing in the 2025 season? If you do, you are either a “Rain Man” or a diabolical liar, as he touched the ball 20 total times before bowing out for the rest of the season to an MCL sprain. He is a man-child and an impressive physical specimen, but likely nothing more than a dart throw in your drafts.

After signing a three-year extension following a tumultuous offseason, it is clear Breece remains the Jets’ main guy in the backfield. The opportunities to score were slim in 2025 as the Jets were tied or trailing on 93% of their offensive snaps, the worst rate in the league. Zoom out a bit further, and you will see that the team ranked dead last in rush attempts inside the 5-yard line for the third year in a row. His volume and breakaway run rate can make up for the team’s shortcomings. With a 45+ reception floor, Hall can be a valuable RB2 and potentially finish as an RB1 if the TDs finally fall in his favor. Early drafters will need to be tracking Hall's health closely over the next couple of weeks, however. He exited practice on August 17 with a groin injury and could miss multiple weeks in training camp.

As CMC’s backup last year in San Francisco, “BRob” totaled just 104 opportunities, including a meager eight receptions. His biggest contribution to fantasy this year could likely be when some dumb-dumb in your league accidentally drafts him in Round 1 as “B. Robinson- RB, ATL”. Tyler Allgeier vacates 160 opportunities, so expect the big-bodied back to mix in occasionally in short-yardage situations for Atlanta. Still, he should not have much standalone value behind Bijan.

While the majority of 2025 fantasy RBs stayed healthy, Irving dealt with foot and shoulder injuries, limiting him to just 10 games. He was extremely ineffective, ranking 51st in rush success rate and 47th in explosive rush rate among 55 qualifying RBs. The Buccaneers also failed to give him a single carry inside the 5-yard line all season! We still believe in the talent, but Irving is shaping up to be one of the bigger wildcard picks in the early rounds. Kenneth Gainwell will certainly steal passing downs work, and Sean Tucker was re-signed to be the Bucs’ red-zone hammer. If you still are bullish on Bucky, shoot your shot as your team’s RB2 in hopes the entire offense resets in 2026.

How good was the Skatt man for the 10 weeks of the season? He was the RB10, averaging 14.5 fantasy points per game, including a month’s stretch where the Giants fed him the ball 22+ times a game. His gruesome ankle fracture was tough to watch, as his energy and enthusiasm made him one of our favorite players to watch in 2025. He came out saying he would be ready for Week 1, but we would expect his best football to be played in the back half of the season, as it may take time to regain his explosiveness and dynamic ability. Consider him an RB2 for your fantasy squads on a run-heavy Giants team with an improved offensive line and a new scheme.

It looked like Brown might end up one of 2025’s biggest fantasy busts after averaging just 8.1 fantasy points per game on 51 total yards through the first five weeks of the season. He ended up becoming a league winner en route to seeing the fourth-most targets among all RBs while averaging 100 total yards per game from Week 6 on. The only yellow flag in his profile is his lack of major success inside the 5-yard line. Cincinnati failed to bring in any other significant RB competition, making Brown yet again a candidate to finish as an RB1 for the third year in a row as part of this Joe Burrow-led offense.

The RB2 job is up for grabs with Emanuel Wilson now in Seattle. Marshawn Lloyd looks to be the next man up, but he has just six carries to his name in the NFL, as he has dealt with injuries for two years straight. If he cannot stay healthy again, Brooks could be in line for the RB2 role for a good offense with Josh Jacobs' legal situation playing out. He is a dart throw in your drafts, knowing the team also traded for former Steelers third-round RB Kaleb Johnson.

CROD! The former Commanders RB quietly ranked fourth among all qualifying RBs in rush success rate and trailed only Bijan Robinson in yards after contact per attempt last season. If you want to connect a few dots, he played his college ball at Kentucky, where Liam Coen was the OC; in that season, he logged 238 touches as the lead ball carrier. He hasn't really done much in the NFL thus far, but the familiarity in Coen's system at least adds some threat to Bhayshul Tuten's early-down role in 2026. Consider him a solid bench stash in your drafts, hoping he finds his way to FLEX value for your teams.

This is the stuff fantasy dreams are made of. If you called your shot with CMC in 2025, oh baby, were you living large while the rest of your league mates cowered in fear due to “he’s gonna get injured” fears. The RB1 was a consistency monster as essentially two players in one for fantasy. Using only his receiving stats, he would have been the WR11 in half-point leagues or the WR8 in full PPR. He tied Amon-Ra St. Brown for the league lead in red zone receptions while totaling a whopping 413 touches, the most by a fantasy RB since DeMarco Murray in 2014. Whew! That type of workload suggests some regression is coming for the 30-year-old, but we still have him ranked as a top-5 RB. He is him, and his skill set for fantasy is like none other since the LaDanian Tomlinson days.

The 27-year-old Chuba finds himself as the presumed lead back in Carolina a year after taking a backseat to Rico Dowdle. The efficiency numbers weren’t pretty, averaging a paltry 3.8 yards per carry with only 6% of his runs gaining 10+ yards, the fourth lowest rate among qualifying RBs. Hubbard will face some competition from former second-round pick Jonathon Brooks, and now he's dealing with a hamstring injury in training camp. Initially, our projections had Hubbard seeing the lion's share of the work for the Panthers, but that projection could change if Brooks keeps showing out in camp.

Over the last six years, only two RBs finished inside the top 24 at the position every year: Derrick Henry and D'Andre Swift. Yep, it isn’t always the sexiest outcomes, but Swift is the clear lead back for a Chicago offense we want pieces of in fantasy. He set career highs in rushing yards, rushing TDs, and rush success rate behind a much- improved Bears offensive line. Over the back half of the season, he did cede work to Kyle Monangai, but we still view Swift as the lead guy in a 60-40 backfield. Does he make it seven years in a row as an RB2? Our projections certainly think so.

The Texans must have a type: past-their-prime early down runners who can be effective scoring TDs in bunches. Montgomery's value received a major boost when he was traded from Detroit to Houston as the team was desperately searching for an answer inside the red zone. The team converted a league-worst 17% of their attempts inside the 5-yard line into TDs, with the league-average being 39%. Monty should see 18+ touches a game and return low-end RB2 value for a team that wants to win by running the ball and leaning on their defense. Claiborne slipped to the sixth round, albeit in a solid landing spot for the future, as both Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason are in the final year of their deals. His experience as a kick returner shows on the field, but dear Lord, Claiborne needs to take care of the football. He frequently was stuffed at the line of scrimmage, fumbled the football, or had concentration issues in the passing game.

You can tell your grandkids you lived through the glory years known as "Derrick Henry SZN". He is an absolute fantasy legend finishing 2025 with his eighth straight season of double-digit rushing TDs. He saw the most carries inside the 5-yard line of his career and ranked third among all RBs in yards per carry. “Father Time” is usually undefeated when it comes to 30+ year old RBs, but Henry has kicked him outside the wrestling ring the last couple of years. Our projections still have him ranked as a low-end RB1 with a slight deduction in full PPR leagues.

The sixth-round pick in 2025 barely sniffed the field for the first three months of the season behind veteran Alvin Kamara. However, he was called upon for a three-week stretch (Weeks 12-14) when he averaged 17 opportunities per My Guy Sleeper Breakout Value Rookie Bust Injury Concerns Colety Crusaders Redraft Rankings 9/2/2026 game before missing the final two weeks of the season due to an injury. Perhaps he can carve out a role as the RB2 behind Etienne as the insurance back, but he is best left on waivers to start the year.

Entering the final year of his free agent deal with the Giants, “Singlecarry” was surpassed on the depth chart by both Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy while seeing career lows in receptions and yards per carry. It’s not the way you want things to trend entering your age-29 season. Consider this man D-O-N-E.

Coming off one of the most consistent fantasy seasons for an RB of all-time, hopefully, any doubts you had about Achane should be buried deep in the ground. He became one of four RBs ever to score 11+ fantasy points in every single game and ranked #1 in yards per carry (5.7) and explosive rush rate (10%) among all qualifying RBs. When you mix in his receiving work, he is a cheat code at the position. Despite Miami’s low win expectation for 2026, we are still in on his price tag at the 1/2 turn in draft as a locked-in RB1.

The former fifth-round pick is the presumed backup to Jonathan Taylor in Indy. However, we confess that his rookie season does not give us a ton of information to work from, as he touched the ball 26 total times and was active in three total games from Week 8 on. He is an explosive athlete with the opportunity to lock up the RB2 spot. For now, know the name, but the JTT manager should not feel obligated to draft him even as insurance.

The second RB taken by the Browns in last year’s draft had a weird rookie campaign. Sampson surprisingly had eight receptions in Week 1 and totaled 40 targets as a change-of-pace back. Yet, he averaged just 2.7 yards per carry and failed to score on the ground. The Browns’ offense will receive a makeover in 2026 with new play-caller Todd Monken and an influx of new receivers. Once lead back Quinshon Judkins returns from his ankle injury, Sampson likely will fade to being a bench stash only in deep PPR leagues.

Wilson was quietly better than Josh Jacobs on a number of efficiency metrics. He is coming off a career high 142 total opportunities in Green Bay and flashed in a major way with his lone start in Week 12 with Jacobs sidelined. His addition to the Seattle backfield is noteworthy given Kenneth Walker’s departure and Zach Charbonnet’s ACL tear. There is a massive opportunity up for grabs in this Seahawks backfield, although first-round pick Jadarian Price will be the lead back with George Holani as the RB2. Expect Wilson to mix in here and there, but he's not on the redraft radar.

Many thought Demercado was signed to fill out the KC backfield behind Kenneth Walker III, but he was cut in late August then claimed off waivers by the Cowboys after Dallas cut Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah. He did quietly have some electric moments through his first three years in the league highlighted by a robust 6.5 yards per carry. Among RBs with at least 125 carries over the last decade, that ranks #1 although the actual fantasy impact has been minimal. He will probably begin the season as the RB3 behind Javonte and Malik Davis, so there's no fantasy value here outside of injury.
current_alert_summary: Claimed by Dallas to help fill the RB depth void left by Jaydon Blue's release; Malik Davis remains the primary backup to starter Javonte Williams.

udk_analysis: Johnson slowly made it into the good graces of Nebraska HC Matt "Ha" Rhule, morphing into one of college football's premier workhorses in 2025. His rough combine metrics hurt his stock as he fell all the way to KC in the fifth round, way behind his projected draft position among consensus boards. He is the classic production-versus-combine metrics discussion at the RB position and now finds himself firmly behind Kenneth Walker III with the Chiefs cutting ties with Emari Demercado.

GEORGE! The Seahawks special teamer was thrust into a bigger role during the NFL playoffs after Zach Charbonnet went down with his ACL tear. He caught three passes in the NFC title game but will once again be relegated to third or fourth string on the roster. Rookie Jadarian Price should work ahead of George, with Charbonnet eventually returning from injury, but until Charbs gets healthy, Holani will have a role as a change-of-pace option.

Davis is an explosive backup RB who averaged 5.5 yards per carry through two seasons, albeit on just 73 total attempts. He was also electric in the passing game, but averaged just 29% of the snaps behind Breece Hall. New OC Frank Reich and HC Aaron Glenn have toiled with the idea of a committee approach, but the contract extension and talent of Hall suggest otherwise. Expect a handful of touches per game but zero fantasy relevance to start the season.

After a solid 2023 campaign, it has been all downhill since for Pacheco after suffering a brutal fibula injury in 2024 and essentially being irrelevant for fantasy in 2025. The veteran signed a one-year deal to replace David Montgomery and his 34 red zone carries. Pacheco’s efficiency numbers are downright disgusting, but opportunity is everything in fantasy. He has been left for dead in ADP, but the setup seems ideal: the clear RB2 on a good offense that can handle a three-down workload if needed. The Lions are favored in a ton of games, so it would not be surprising if Pacheco returned low-end FLEX value this year once he gets healthy. He's set to miss multiple weeks in camp because of a sprained MCL, but he should be ready for Week 1.
current_alert_summary: Signed by Detroit in free agency (left Kansas City); placed on IR (~Sept 1, 2026) with an MCL sprain and back injury from training camp; eligible to return for Detroit's Week 5 game vs Arizona.

udk_analysis: With Isiah Pacheco being placed on IR to start the season, Saylors looks like the backup to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit after Dan Campbell announced that he was comfortable with him as their No. 2. We'll be honest: his TWO total career carries do not give us a ton work from if you are asking "how talented is he?" Roster him as the Lions insurance back if you have space on your roster.

BILL CROSKEY! The subject of Footballers fame burst onto the scene last summer as a seventh-round NFL draft pick and ultimately lost his starting job to Chris Rodriguez Jr. He converted just three of his 12 carries inside the 5-yard line to TDs last year and now finds more competition in the backfield with Rachaad White’s signing and rookie Kaytron Allen. While things look good on paper for Bill entering 2026, this is a buyer-beware situation. Washington is favored in just two of its first 10 games.

After much speculation before the NFL Draft, the Seahawks took the Notre Dame RB with the final pick of Round 1. Price’s selection looks even stronger, knowing we did not see another RB drafted until the end of Round 3. His initial burst plus his contact balance make for a lethal combo, although he was not utilized much in the passing game in college, with just 15 total receptions over three years. With Zach Charbonnet on the mend from an ACL injury, Price found arguably the best landing spot for a rookie RB in 2026. The Seahawks are favored in each of their first 10 matchups. We have him ranked as a high-end FLEX/RB2 option with the expectation that his draft stock could rise as get closer to Week 1.

Perhaps our small brains cannot comprehend this man’s greatness in fantasy football. Gibbs is a superstar, totaling the most TDs (49) in NFL history by any RB through their first three years in the NFL. After Dan Campbell took over as play-caller (Week 10), Gibbs had the seventh most receptions of any player in the NFL as David Montgomery was phased out of the offense. Gibbs should see the biggest workload of his career and is a worthy selection at 1.01 this year. Consider your opponent’s pants pee-stained every time he touches the ball.

It has been a wonderful run for Conner, but it seems he finally will fade into the fantasy background. After four straight years as a top-20 RB and the engine of the Arizona offense, the 31-year-old missed the majority of 2025 with a right foot injury and will begin on injured reserve. It seems he will be buried on the depth chart behind Tyler Allgeier and rookie Jeremiyah Love.
current_alert_summary: Placed on IR (designation to return) Aug 30, 2026 while still working back from a severe 2025 season-ending foot/ankle injury; must miss a minimum of 4 games, earliest eligible return Week 5 (Oct 11 vs Detroit).

udk_analysis: After agreeing to a four-year contract extension in mid-August, James Cook punched every "TD-regression" metric in the face in 2025, leading the league in rushing yards and finishing as a top-6 fantasy back. He paced the league with 11 games of 80+ yards rushing and ranked 3rd in yards after contact. The only stain on Cook’s resume is his declining involvement in the passing game, as he averaged just 1.9 receptions per game last year. Fantasy managers can have confidence in the continuity of this Buffalo offense, the play-calling, and an offensive line that continues to maul opposing fronts. Cook remains a strong RB1 for us in 2026.

One of the best fantasy stories of 2025 had to be the resurgence of Javonte Williams as Dallas' RB1. Among qualified RBs, Javonte was fourth in yards after contact per attempt while seeing 19 opportunities per game. For the first four years of his frustrating career, he had eight total TDs inside the 5-yard line; in 2025, he had 10! With no direct competition for touches, Javonte is a solid RB2 as part of a Dallas offense we love buying into for fantasy.

Blue was a hyped name last summer as a fifth-round rookie, and some claimed could take hold of the Dallas backfield. Whoops! He took a backseat to Javonte Williams while being inactive in 12 games last season. The Cowboys ultimately decided to cut Blue in late August, opening up the door for Malik Davis to take command of the RB2 role. After being cut, the Eagles signed Blue to their practice squad.
current_alert_summary: Cowboys waived 2025 fifth-round RB Blue on Aug 30, 2026, citing practice-habit/maturity concerns (per HC Brian Schottenheimer), despite him entering camp as the presumptive No. 2 RB behind Javonte Williams. Remained an unsigned free agent as of Sept 1, 2026.

udk_analysis: Warren had a high floor throughout the season, averaging 16 opportunities per game and 12.3 fantasy points per game while receiving a “B” in our consistency metrics. While he ceded passing downs work to Kenneth Gainwell down the stretch, it was the best fantasy season of Warren’s four-year career, thanks to an increase in workload. He was rather pedestrian inside the 5-yard line, converting only four of his 14 carries. His outlook for 2026 is souring with the signing of Rico Dowdle and the arrival of a new coaching regime. He is stuck in a complicated backfield mess, profiling more as a FLEX, knowing he could take a backseat to Dowdle at some point.

After two seasons backing up De’Von Achane in Miami, it is clear Wright is not cut from the same cloth. He was drafted for his speed (4.38 40-time), but is averaging only 3.9 yards per carry and caught eight total passes. He is a backup RB on a team currently favored in just one of their 17 games. Translation: he is not on our redraft radar.

The Notre Dame superstar became the highest draft RB since Saquon Barkley after the Cardinals selected him third overall. His combination of size, speed, early breakout age (19.3), and production is a recipe for success at the next level. Tyler Allgeier could steal some goal-line looks and temper expectations for fantasy. His weekly workload will be in question despite the fact that RBs drafted inside the top 10 have averaged 19+ touches per game in Year 1 over the last decade. We have Love ranked as an RB2 for 2026, but his Week 1 outlook is now in question. He exited Arizona's first preseason game with a high ankle sprain and is expected to miss the remainder of the preseason.
current_alert_summary: Rookie RB (No. 3 overall pick) suffered a high ankle sprain in his preseason debut (Aug 16, 2026); ruled out the rest of preseason. HC Mike LaFleur has not guaranteed Week 1 (Sept 13 vs LAC) availability. With James Conner also out to start the year, this creates real uncertainty atop Arizona's back

udk_analysis: Poor J.K… can this guy catch a break? Through the first ten weeks of the season, he was the RB18, averaging 16.7 opportunities per game ahead of the more hyped RJ Harvey. An unfortunate “hip-drop” tackle ended his season yet again, as he now has appeared in just 38% of possible games over the last five years. He signed a two-year deal worth up to $20 million to run it back with the Broncos. While we still expect Harvey to see high-value looks in the pass game, Dobbins should have FLEX-worthy weeks in the right matchup while running behind one of the best offensive lines in football.

With an early breakout age (20) and 25 rushing TDs over his final two seasons, he was the engine of the Huskies offense post-Michael Penix Jr. years. Coleman’s draft stock slipped after a lack of testing, but the landing spot in Denver should put him on your radar. Sean Payton loves utilizing an RB committee more than his own family, as Coleman begins the season third or fourth on the RB depth chart. Keep your head on a swivel, knowing Coleman could have a moment as a priority waiver pickup.

Oh man, those first 10 weeks of JTT were legendary! His five 30+ fantasy point games were tied with 2000 Marshall Faulk and 2006 LaDanian Tomlinson for the most ever through the first ten weeks of a season. As a receiver, he was more involved than ever, setting career highs in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Unfortunately, the Colts’ offense tanked down the stretch with Philip Rivers & Riley Leonard under center. Taylor’s production essentially was cut in half, nosediving from 23.3 fantasy points per game with Daniel Jones to 11.8 over those final five games. JTT is still a locked-in RB1 for us, although the first month of the season is a brutal stretch for the Colts.

Brooks enters his age-23 season with 12 total touches over two seasons since he was taken 46th overall. We have not seen him on the football field since Week 14 of the 2024 season after he brutally re-injured his ACL. Monitor training camp news and beat reporters to see how involved he could be in 2026. Rico Dowdle vacates 51% of the carries and 10% of the team’s targets, giving credence to Brooks being a sleeper name to stash at the end of your drafts. We always loved the talent, but for now, we still have projected behind Chuba Hubbard in Carolina.

Wait, we are mentioning a former fifth-round RB who was on the field for three total offensive snaps in 2025? The San Francisco backfield annually gives us relevant fantasy backup RBs who seemingly come out of nowhere: Raheem Mostert, Jeff Wilson Jr., Eli Mitchell, and Jordan Mason ring a bell? The 49ers beat reporters seem to suggest James could enter the mix for the backup role behind Christian McCaffrey this year, despite having as many career regularseason carries as your grandmother. Know the name and be willing to draft him as CMC insurance if you want to be cautious.

Mason continues to show he belongs in the NFL, averaging 5.1 yards per carry since coming into the league in 2022. For context, only De’Von Achane (5.6) and Jahmyr Gibbs (5.3) are higher in that span. After averaging 16 opportunities per game through the first six games, he eventually fell behind Aaron Jones Sr. in the RB rotation down the stretch in a lost season for the Vikings. Mason is older than you might realize (27 years old), but is only an injury away from being an every-down workhorse.

It looked like Jacobs was going to repeat as a certifiable RB1 for fantasy, averaging 22 opportunities and 1.2 rushing TDs per game through the first ten weeks of the season. He hit a major wall down the stretch, dealing with a knee injury and averaging just 10.5 fantasy points from Week 13 on. We know what he is: a TD monster with a league-leading 24 rushing TDs inside the 10-yard line over the last two seasons. If he is on the field, the workload should be there.... but now he's got a serious legal situation. Jacobs was formally charged with two misdemeanors related to his May arrest and was recently placed on the commissioner's exemption list. He Is now a risky pick in drafts given the off-the-field issues and the variables about how long he could be suspended.
current_alert_summary: Placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List (Aug 30, 2026) after being charged with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property from a May 2026 incident; cannot practice, attend games, or be on the active roster while on the list (though still paid). No suspension length formally an

udk_analysis: Hill averaged 5.2 yards per carry in limited work before suffering a neck injury in Week 12 and not returning to the field in 2025. He continues to be a “better in real life football” back as a valuable third-down pass protector. This is a new regime in Baltimore, so Hill’s playing time in 2026 could certainly dip. He does not sniff FLEX-worthy territory even in full PPR leagues.

Despite a lackluster production profile, Black was a hot commodity in pre-draft visits, meeting with 10 teams before the 49ers surprisingly selected him 90th overall. Kyle Shanahan offenses always surprise us with the names that leap from obscurity, but this one was a head scratcher. CMC is coming off a season where he touched the ball 413 times, so perhaps we see Black worked into the mix. Pay attention to camp reports to see where he lands on the depth chart, competing with Jordan James and Isaac Guerendo for backup duties. 72 Jerome Ford (FA)

Should we just act like 2025 never happened? The Steelers drafted Johnson in the third round, and then it was all downhill from there. His kickoff blunder in Week 1 against Seattle set the stage for a train-wreck of a season where he was inactive in seven games and failed to have a single rush attempt gain 10+ yards. If there is any hope for the future, it is the fact that Mike Tomlin is gone, and Mike McCarthy could give him a clean slate. He begins the off-season as the projected RB3 in Pittsburgh.
current_alert_summary: Acquired by Green Bay from Pittsburgh (for a 2028 6th-round pick) on Aug 30, 2026, directly in response to Josh Jacobs being placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List; expected to share early-season backfield work with MarShawn Lloyd.

udk_analysis: Nicknamed "the Fatman" by his mother, Allen came into Penn State as a highly regarded recruit and got to work in the gym. He checks a lot of the physical profile boxes we want at the next level, and finished his college career as Penn State's all-time leader in rush attempts and rushing yards. The question is whether his lack of flash and creativity as a runner will cap him at the next level. He likely begins third or fourth on the Washington depth chart.

Keaton Mitchell had some moments in Baltimore as an explosive home run hitter, but he never developed into an every-down player thanks to some injuries and a random guy named Derrick Henry. Now in LA, Mitchell should be battling with Kimani Vidal for the RB2 role behind Omarion Hampton. The Chargers just invested a first-round pick in Hampton a year ago, so we are projecting him as the bell cow. That doesn’t leave much fantasy value for a guy like Mitchell in standard redraft leagues, but he could end up being one of fantasy’s premier insurance policies if he beats out Vidal for the backup role.

Ken Bone! Walker was a key piece of the Seattle offense down the stretch and parlayed his Super Bowl MVP award by receiving a big old bag of money from the Chiefs. He signed a three-year deal worth just over $14M per year. He is still only 25 years old and remains one of the best home run hitters in the game, something that was severely lacking in KC's run game over the last two years. For context, over the last two years, Chiefs RBs have run for 10+ yards less than 9% of the time, 31st amongst 32 teams. Enter Walker, who was third in the league last season in rate of 10+ yard runs and #1 in forced missed tackle rate. Expect 18-20 touches per game as the team re-establishes the run game and the red zone approach under OC Eric Bienemy en route to RB1 status for the Bone Zone.

It pays to be in Aaron Rodgers' inner circle, just ask Kenny G! He signed a one-year deal last off-season after spending the first part of his career in Philly as a third-down back and kick returner. Of course, most of us were not expecting much from Gainwell given his track record and the minimal investment, but goodness gracious, he was a force in PPR formats thanks to his team-leading 73 receptions. The only backs with more catches? CMC, Bijan, and Jahmyr Gibbs. He is a valuable commodity as a FLEX option, especially if Bucky Irving fails to regain his rookie-year form.

Vidal Sassoon! To this man’s credit, he went from being inactive in the first few games behind Omarion Hampton and Najee Harris to becoming one of the more valuable adds off the waiver wire in 2025. After Harris went down for the season and Hampton suffered a serious ankle injury, Vidal stepped in as the lead back and finished as a top-24 fantasy RB in five of eight games where he played 60+ percent of the snaps. It is nice to know that if the opportunity arises, he is fully capable of handling 15+ touches as a plug-and-play option. Of course, we are not projecting much workload with Omarion Hampton atop the depth chart and Keaton Mitchell joining the squad in free agency, so he is not worth a draft pick, but if Hampton happens to go down, he will be a priority add off the waiver wire.

The seventh-round Monangai was a revelation, tag-teaming with Swift as the Bears posted the sixth-most total rushing yards in the league. Monangai was a machine, gaining 5+ yards on 42.6% of his carries, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only Kyren Williams. He certainly has juice with the upside to see a big workload if Swift went down, as evidenced by a Week 9 game where Ben Johnson turned full sicko, feeding Monangai the ball 31(!) times. Consider Monangai a “FLEX with benefits” later in your draft.
current_alert_summary: Hyperextended his knee in an Aug 16, 2026 practice; ESPN reported he's expected to miss 'multiple weeks.' Not placed on IR at final cuts but remained week-to-week and DNP into late August, leaving Week 1 (Sept 13 vs Carolina) uncertain.

udk_analysis: Ever since Sean McVay gave Kyren the reins, he has been amazing for fantasy, finishing as a top-10 back in three straight seasons. He is rarely hitting big plays or flashing elite speed in the open field, but he is as dependable as they come, and McVay trusts this dude. Blake Corum is probably going to steal a few TDs and work in for a handful of touches per game, but when the game is on the line, McVay is calling Kyren’s number. In 2026, he is projected as a volume-based high-end RB2 who could bank another RB1 finish if the TDs go his way.

The 2025 7th round pick had 33 total touches his rookie year mixing in sparingly as a third down back. With Travis Etienne Jr. now in New Orleans, perhaps Allen carves out a bigger role alongside Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. For now, he is simply a name to know, not someone to draft even in the deepest of leagues.

If you are looking for the RB2 behind Javonte Williams, look no further. The former undrafted free agent has stuck around Dallas bouncing between practice squad and being buried on the depth chart the last few years before showing out in limited opportunities last year. He balled out when Javonte Williams missed Week 17 going for 103 rushing yards against the Commanders. Consider him the insurance RB to roster for a high-powered offense.
current_alert_summary: With Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah both off the roster, Davis is the Cowboys' primary backup RB to starter Javonte Williams, making him a notable late-round handcuff.

udk_analysis: The 88th overall pick in 2024 had seven total touches through two years as his body continues to betray him, but he has made it through camp without an injury (knock on wood). Seriously, can this guy make it from practice to the NFL field? So far, so good - and now Josh Jacobs' off-the-field issues make him an intriguing play. The fact that the Packers didn't take a single RB in the NFL Draft for the second straight year suggests the team was still envisioning him for the RB2 role behind Jacobs as he becomes one of the premier insurance backs in drafts. We have docked Jacobs in projections, and depending on how long he is suspended, we consider Lloyd a plug-and-play RB2. Feel free to reach a round or two in ADP, as his draft price probably won't account for the full range of outcomes.
current_alert_summary: With Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List, Lloyd is currently positioned as Green Bay's early-down back to open the season, splitting work with newly-acquired Kaleb Johnson.

udk_analysis: If you are looking for a “big-bodied back” from this class, Big Mike might be your style. He blew the doors off the combine but landed on a Vegas team that has franchise RB Ashton Jeanty blocking his path to fantasy relevance. New HC Klint Kubiak did utilize a two-back system in Seattle, so perhaps Washington works his way into the rotation more than we realize, especially after showing out in the preseason. We view him as one of the higher priority insurance RBs, especially after Ashton Jeanty picked up an ankle injury in late August.

The veteran back signed with the Giants as a late camp addition but seems to be gaining the trust of the coaching staff. He is way past the good ole days when he was a workhorse for fantasy but it should not be shocking if he eats into My Guy Sleeper Breakout Value Rookie Bust Injury Concerns Colety Crusaders Redraft Rankings 9/2/2026 Cam Skattebo's workload. Consider Najee either a stash in deeper leagues or a waiver name to monitor over the first few weeks.

The former #1 RB recruit in the nation finished his four-year career at Penn State as Penn State's all-time rushing TD leader with 45! Unfortunately, after suffering a foot injury during a Senior Bowl practice, Singleton's draft stock fell to the fifth round. If you believe in his size/speed combo, perhaps he can eventually overtake Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears and turn into a team's lead back in the back half of the season.

The 6’2” bruiser saw limited work as a rookie, averaging an utterly disgusting 2.8 yards per carry on 70 total carries. Sounds bad, right? What if we told you that was the WORST per carry average of any rookie RB over the last decade? Seriously, 99 different rookie RBs since 2016 saw 70+ carries, and Ollie was the worst. It was quite the dubious distinction. Are you curious who the best rookie was in that span? (Seriously, since you are here wanting Ollie Gordon II takes, we might as well keep this thing rolling.) It was some guy named De’Von Achane who averaged five MORE yards per carry (7.8) than Ollie did. His sixth-round draft capital, Achane’s insane talent, and the Dolphins' projected win total (4.5) suggest you will not be counting on Ollie in 2026.

It was a frustrating rookie season for Omarion Hampton, who missed Weeks 6-13 with a small fracture in his ankle. However, when he was on the field, you saw flashes of what he can do in fantasy. He only appeared in nine games, but in those contests, Hampton handled a 30% share of the team’s total rush attempts and targets. For context, anything at or above 30% in that metric is elite and quite rare. Now entering Year 2 in the league, there is room for that number to grow, and if it does in this Mike McDaniel scheme with a healthier offensive line, Hampton is a strong candidate to finish inside the top 10 at the position.

Judkins was everything the Browns envisioned when they selected him 34th overall in last year’s draft. Despite the team’s lack of success, he was a workhorse, averaging 18.3 touches per game and 34% of the team's total rush attempts and targets before a brutal dislocated ankle and fractured fibula ended his season in Week 16. He has a chance to be cleared for Week 1, though he will not be 100% when the season begins. Expect his production to pick up in the second half of the season, making him an awkward selection in the middle rounds of your draft.

'Dick White,' as he's known around TFFB HQ, is going to be donning new colors in 2026 after spending the first four years of his career in Tampa. White was the guy a couple of seasons ago, but he was relegated to a change-of-pace option with the emergence of the more efficient Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker over the last two years. For context, his opportunities per game have declined from 20.1 to 12.6 to 10.4 over the last three seasons. We know his place as a pass-catcher, and he might be going overlooked in drafts despite our projections having him as a FLEX option.

After a steady rookie season backing up James Cook, Davis saw his usage curiously cut in half last year, averaging just 15% of the snaps and just four touches per game despite dressing for all 17 regular-season games. He is nothing more than an insurance policy for Cook managers as he fights for playing time alongside third-down back Ty Johnson.

Stevenson finished the season as the RB25, thanks to the final three weeks of the season, where he scored six TDs despite averaging just 11 touches per game. He was quietly a pass-catching fiend throughout the year, leading all RBs in yards per target (9.3) and a thorn in the side of TreVeyon Henderson truthers. This regime seems more confident in Stevenson in pass protection, as we expect this to remain a 50-50 timeshare. He is a FLEX option to start the year on a Patriots team that will have a much tougher schedule in 2026.

After Chuba Hubbard was hurt in Week 5 last year, Rico essentially stole the RB1 role in Carolina; he was highly productive with his opportunities, mixing in some wild 30+ fantasy point spike weeks. Mr. "Two Pumps" Dowdle rushed for 1,076 yards this past season and ran for a career high six TDs as the leader of the committee in Carolina. Dowdle has been the lead guy for two different teams now, and while he may not be an elite talent, the guy just gets the job done. He lands in Pittsburgh reunited with former coach Mike McCarthy alongside Jaylen Warren. Consider Rico a “FLEX with benefits” to start the year.

It was a slow start for the second-round rookie as he averaged just 8.5 opportunities per game behind J.K. Dobbins through the first ten weeks of the season. However, after Dobbins went down with yet another season-ending injury, Harvey averaged 18.4 opportunities, 17 fantasy points per game, and finished the season with 12 total TDs. Those scores might be propping him up in fantasy managers’ minds despite the fact that his efficiency marks were less than stellar as a runner. Sean Payton seems committed to a RB committee, bringing back J.K. Dobbins while adding fourth- round pick Jonah Coleman. Harvey is in FLEX territory, but he might be maddening as a start/sit decision every week.

Old man Samaje Perine is in his final year under contract solely to annoy Chase Brown managers. He averaged seven opportunities per game last season, thanks to running more routes and catching more balls on third down than Brown. For redraft purposes, he is off our boards.

Coming off a legendary 2024 campaign and Super Bowl run, there were warning signs about regression coming across the board for Saquon and the Eagles' offense. He bottomed out in a number of areas, including plummeting from 17 runs of 20+ yards to only four in 2025. He also shockingly converted only one of his 13 carries inside the 5-yard line into a TD, but still volumed his way to finishing as the RB13. With an offensive coordinator change, we expect Saquon to bounce back in 2026 at a discounted price in the second round of your drafts. Your league mates might bring up the fact he was a “bust,” but we are willing to forgive and forget.

Tucker had a few shining moments in 2025, including a monster RB1 overall performance in Buffalo in Week 11. He can flash at times and also led the team in carries (14) and rushing TDs (6) inside the 10-yard line. However, the Buccaneers backfield needs to move from a three-headed monster (Bucky, Kenny G & the Tuckmeister) to two in order for him to be started with any confidence. Expect Tucker to be floating on waiver wires after your drafts.

McGowan has been around the block, starting out at Oklahoma way back in 2020, being in jail for three months, and out of football for two years, playing at Butler junior college in 2023, New Mexico State in 2024, and finally, Kentucky in 2025. Whew. Did you get all that? The 7th rounder finished preseason as the presumed backup to Jonathan Taylor. For now, note the name and be ready to pounce on the waiver wire if he is the insurance back to roster.

Taken in the sixth round in 2025, there were rumblings that Brooks could win the backup job behind Chase Brown. (Narrator: but he did not.) The Day 3 pick touched the ball 17 total times as a rookie, and old man Samaje Perine is back again in 2026 as the trusted third-down back the Bengals mix in.

There are those out there clamoring for more Tank touches as the Eagles’ backup RB averaged 5.7 yards per carry playing behind the same offensive line Saquon Barkley did in 2025. Bigsby was acquired after Week 1 and did not sniff double-digit touches in a game until Week 15. With just 11 career receptions, he remains in a niche role as an early down thumper behind one of the league’s most talented backs. You can certainly add him to your roster with one of your final picks as an insurance policy.

Pollard might have been the most boring fantasy selection at RB in 2025. The first 13 weeks were utter garbage as he averaged 15+ touches per game while turning that volume into a measly 7.9 fantasy points per game. Woof. He did save the best for last, turning it on in the final month of the fantasy season with four top-20 finishes in a row while averaging 113 rushing yards per game. The 29-year-old is hitting the crashing point in the lifecycle of an NFL RB and enters the final year of his Titans contract as the lead back on an offense that hopefully takes a step forward under new OC Brian Daboll. If dirty, dirty RB volume is your thing, Pollard can be a FLEX for your team for one last ride in 2026.

After Jacksonville’s Week 8 bye, Etienne turned into a fantasy force, averaging 17.5 fantasy points per game as the RB7. He was a wild outlier as a pass-catcher, becoming the third RB over the last 25 years to score 6+ rec TDs on fewer than 40 receptions. The main headline for the man formerly known as Travis Etienne Jr. was the four-year free agent deal he signed to come home to New Orleans and be crowned Travis “Aychane” Jr. With Alvin Kamara phasing out of the team’s plans, Etienne will be given every opportunity to be a workhorse for this Kellen Moore-designed offense. While the Saint’s weekly TD expectation might be low, he should end up a solid RB2 on volume alone.

Stop if you have heard this before: we love us some Hendo. It was a painfully slow start to his career, but he broke out in the second half as the RB8 from Week 9 on, averaging 16.7 fantasy points per game. When Rhamondre Stevenson was out for a month, he showcased bell cow capabilities, averaging 20+ opportunities per game and an 80% snap rate. We know he is explosive, but will the coaching staff trust him as the team’s main passing-downs back in 2026? He carries massive upside at his ADP, but we would recommend building out RB depth on your roster around him as you navigate the beginning of the season with Hendo.

Travis’ little brother was a fourth-rounder out of Georgia last year who touched the ball only 23 times as a rookie. He will compete with Jonathon Brooks for touches behind Chuba Hubbard. That is fantasy football code for: he is probably irrelevant.

The 25-year-old enters the final year of his rookie contract stuck in no man’s land for fantasy. Tony Pollard eats up the majority of early down work, and the Titans offense routinely fails to convert long drives. In fact, Tennessee was tied or trailing on 84% of their offensive snaps in 2025, with only the Jets and Saints being worse. You would think that would translate to sweet, sweet Spears garbage time production, but the Titans RB totaled just 14 fantasy points as a third-down receiver all year long. In the deepest of PPR leagues, he makes sense as a bench stash, but he could face more competition for touches with fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton.

Johnson will always mean more to the Buffalo Bills than your fantasy teams. He ranked fifth among all RBs in the NFL in routes run on third down and did see an annoyingly high 23 opportunities inside the red zone. His biggest contribution to fantasy will be watching the TV and screaming that your RB target went to “Johnson” instead of “Cook”. Even in the deepest of PPR leagues, Ty is just a guy.

Poor Tyler. After signing a two-year contract with the Cardinals, the team promptly gave him a proverbial stiff-arm, selecting rookie Jeremiyah Love third overall in the NFL Draft. The 26-year-old bruiser will still make noise inside the red zone after his seven rushing TDs inside the 20-yard line actually outpaced Bijan Robinson last year in Atlanta. However, for redraft purposes, he is nothing more than a bench stash and insurance back for Love managers.

The former college WR was a nice story as a fifth-round pick in 2024 who certainly asserted himself as the most effective RB on a bad Giants team. Fast forward a year, and he was usurped by Cam Skattebo before his season-ending injury. From Week 7 on, Tracy saw a respectable 16.7 opportunities per game and averaged 80+ yards per game. He certainly is capable of being a fantasy-friendly asset thanks to his pass-catching abilities, but we project him to firmly be the RB2 behind Skattebo. In the later rounds of your drafts, we do not mind adding Tracy to your bench if you think they lean on him at the beginning of the year as Skatt ramps up.

Competing with Tank Bigsby for scraps at the table, Shipley had just 23 total touches on the season for 105 total yards. To put his brief two-year career in perspective, his 27% rush success rate ranks 419th among 425 qualifying RBs since 2010. Apologies if you were coming to Will Shipley’s player profile hoping for some optimism. It ain’t here, folks!

After being taken in the fourth round in 2025, Marks saw 17 opportunities per game from Week 7 on. The Texans obviously were not very impressed with the efficiency (3.5 yards per carry) and forced missed tackle rate (54th out of 55 qualifying RBs), leading them to trade for veteran David Montgomery. He returns to being a backup and insurance back option only.

Before suffering a torn ACL in the divisional round against the 49ers, Charbonnet was arguably the better fantasy asset than Kenneth Walker III on the season. His 12 rushing TDs tied James Cook for fifth most among RBs, and he ranked seventh in yards after contact per attempt. It was clear the team trusted him as they entered the red zone with 17% of his carries occurring inside the 10-yard line, the second highest rate of any qualifying RB in the NFL. He will begin the regular season on PUP with the possibility that his recovery extends into October. He is buried in our rankings and someone we are happy to see get drafted by another league mate as they wait for his return.

With Noah Fant out of the picture, the TE position was up for grabs in Seattle, and Barner did a decent job showing he should be the guy moving forward. Finishing as the TE14, he had a decent 64 targets, which turned into 519 yards and six TDs. His 18 looks in the red zone were stellar too, just two fewer than JSN. He remains too volatile in redraft, especially with fellow Seahawk Elijah Arroyo still in the mix. Barner had finishes as high as TE1 and as low as TE58 last year.
