It was a tough 2025 season for the elder statesman, who missed a ton of time with hamstring and collarbone injuries. He will be 33 this season, so be mindful of his ADP throughout the summer. If he gets steamed up, we are hesitant to chase him up the board, but if he falls, there is double-digit TD upside with Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan, especially with George Kittle coming off a torn Achilles and Ricky Pearsall out for the year. Drafters should also be aware that Evans has been battling quad and groin injuries in training camp, and while it doesn't appear he's in danger of missing Week 1, he could be limited leading up to the regular season opener.
current_alert_summary: Signed a 3-year, $60.4M deal with San Francisco this offseason. Dealt with a quad issue in camp, then a groin injury, and missed practice time in late August 2026 while 'planning to play Week 1.' Limited chemistry-building time with new QB Brock Purdy is a real ramp-up concern.

udk_analysis: Even with C.J. Stroud disappointing more often than not from a real-life NFL perspective, Collins continues to post WR1 numbers on a per-game basis. He is just that dude in this offense, and with Tank Dell recovering from a major injury and last year’s rookies, Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel, unproven commodities, Collins’ elite target share remains locked in. He is on the short list of players who are capable of finishing as a top-five fantasy WR in 2026.

The wee little man signed a two-year deal with the Falcons in free agency, and if you have been following the NFL long enough, that probably sounds familiar. He actually began his career with Atlanta as a UDFA back in 2019, so we have a bit of a reunion situation going on here. Quite honestly, there is a chance he sees some playing time given the state of the depth chart behind Drake London. That said, we don’t anticipate him being fantasy relevant as he has been in the league for seven years and has never averaged more than 5.5 fantasy PPG.

How many fantasy options can this version of Geno Smith support in 2026? We know Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall are likely to dominate touches here, so any secondary Jets players are probably going to have to get there via efficiency. Call us crazy, but if your eyeballs saw Geno playing QB last season, we are a little hesitant with that bet! That is where the concern comes in for a guy like Cooper, who profiles as a possession and yards after the catch WR in the NFL. So long as Garrett Wilson is healthy, Cooper’s fantasy upside will be capped, but you could always target him late in drafts and see what shakes out in New York early in the season. Rookie WRs are generally good bets at ADP because the cost is reasonable, but if we are comparing Cooper to the other first-round NFL draft picks, he is not as big of a priority as guys like Carnell Tate, Makai Lemon, or Jordyn Tyson.

Washington went from just a depth piece for Jacksonville to their leading receiver in 2025. Wild times, man! Following the bye week and Travis Hunter’s injury, Washington saw a 23% target share while running roughly half his routes from the slot. We are really interested in taking shots on this Jaguars’ offense, but it is nearly impossible to project the WR usage here, especially with Travis Hunter’s role up in the air. As a result of that uncertainty, expect the Jaguars guys to all be decent values in drafts. There is some downside with each individual WR here, but if you hit on the right guy, the payoff could be massive, especially at these depressed ADPs.

Bryant did very little early in the season, but as the year went on, he started to pop as the team scaled back Troy Franklin’s role. Unfortunately, a concussion and hamstring injury limited his production late in the year, so entering Year 2, there are still question marks on Bryant as a player. He will have a role, but it is highly unlikely to be fantasy relevant now that Jaylen Waddle is on this roster. Consider him a potential waiver wire pickup if Waddle and/or Sutton miss time.

Puka was dominant in 2025 with a league-leading 107 receiving yards per game and six weeks of 20+ fantasy points, the most among WRs. He was an absolute dominator on 50/50 balls, tracking down 27 contested catches, the most of any WR over the last decade. Aside from off-the-field issues, he is simply unstoppable and off-the-charts in every per-route metric we care about for fantasy. If you wanted to take Puka at the 1.01 in a full PPR league, we totally understand.

Only five WRs collected 8+ receiving TDs in each of the last two seasons: Ja’Marr Chase, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Tee Higgins, Davante Adams, and (drumroll)… Quentin Johnston. After previously being the laughingstock of fantasy leagues, he morphed into a solid outside option for Justin Herbert. He led the team in receiving yards (789), deep targets (19), and fantasy points per game (10.4). He may not look appealing on a fantasy roster, but Johnston’s TD upside makes him a worthy second FLEX option, especially in games where the Chargers are favored. He averaged a solid six targets and 11 fantasy points per game in wins the last two seasons

Welp! Another offseason discussing Rashee Rice and his off-the-field issues. Rice missed the first six weeks of the 2025 season while serving a suspension, and this past offseason, he violated his probation when he tested positive for marijuana. As a result, he is serving jail time in June and July. On top of that, we also got news in late May that Rice underwent a “clean up” procedure in his knee that could sideline him for roughly two months. If you recall, Rice’s 2024 season came to an end after he suffered a season-ending LCL, hamstring and posterolateral corner injury. So, to recap, we have another legal issue and a health concern. It all adds up to make Rice a highly volatile player entering training camp, assuming he is cleared. When on the field, he produces like a WR1 for fantasy, but there are obviously concerns. We will be tracking his situation closely over the next few months.
current_alert_summary: Jailed 30 days (released June 16, 2026) for a probation violation tied to his 2024 case; the NFL reviewed this and Rice will NOT face an additional suspension on top of the 6 games he already served in 2025. Expected fully available for Week 1.

For fantasy, things just never got going, however, as he was never a high-volume pass catcher behind JSN and Cooper Kupp. Now with a full offseason in Seattle and a big fat paycheck, perhaps that changes in 2026. We view him as a boom/bust late-round dart, but we do know that he is a fully capable WR who has produced in New Orleans when given the opportunity.

When you are in the last round of your draft, shoot for the moon. Shoot for a guy who hasn’t done it yet in the hopes you find a diamond in the rough. Through five years, Bateman has yet to clear nine fantasy points per game. We will be happy to snag him off the waiver wire in the event of a Zay Flowers injury, but we would prefer to take some swings on younger rookies or insurance RBs late in drafts.

Pittsburgh took Roman Wilson in the third round back in 2024, and after struggling to stay healthy in Year 1, he was just a part time player in 2025. Hey, to his credit, he did finish as the WR8 in Week 8 against the Packers, so he’s got that going for him. #NeverForget. He is likely to be a part-time player again in 2026, who is stuck behind Pitty City, Metcalf, and second-round rookie Germie Bernard.

For the first time in his career, Doubs will not be playing in green and yellow; he signed a lucrative contract in free agency to join Drake Maye and the Patriots. However, the arrival of A.J. Brown puts him back in FLEX territory as a "better for the NFL than fantasy" type of WR. His receiving yards (724) and fantasy points per game (8.6) were a career-high last season but middling marks compared to the rest of fantasy WRs. He should be an every down, outside guy which pushes him to just a bench stash with some FLEX appeal.

Last season was a rollercoaster for Rome Odunze. It feels like forever ago, but remember when Rome was THE WR1 in the first month of the season? The guy was on fire to open the year, but after the team’s bye, he regressed and then got injured, missing Weeks 14-18 with a foot injury. Now entering 2026, there is perhaps a buying window in fantasy as the market is hot and heavy for Luther Burden and Colston Loveland. This is still a former top-10 draft pick, and he is guaranteed to play in 2WR sets for one of the best play-callers in the league. Burden and Loveland feel like the more exciting fantasy picks in Chicago, but Rome outscoring both of those guys is in the range of outcomes.

The clear WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, Flournoy had 11 receptions for 158 yards last season in the three games that Lamb missed. He only gets a second look if Lamb and or Pickens are injured.

The Bills sure do have a type, don’t they? Khalil Shakir and DJ Moore do their best work in the short-to-intermediate area, where they can win after the catch. That is kind of what Bell does best, too, so he is a fit in Joe Brady’s offense. Unfortunately, given that Moore, Shakir, and Josh Palmer are atop the depth chart, we are not sure he will carve out a consistent role as a rookie. 123 Van Jefferson (FA) 30.1 - 37.10 4.0 2.0 47.1 16 89 “Have you seen this WR depth chart behind Terry McLaurin? Someone could see a big opportunity here!” you explain to your friend. Listen up, bud: Van Jeff will be entering his seventh season in the NFL as a certifiable “Cardio King”. He runs the routes, he knows the plays, and yet his 10% career target share reminds you he should not be allowed on a fantasy roster. He has not scored ten fantasy points in a game since 2022!

After one season in New England paired with Drake Maye, the veteran WR finds himself in Washington with Jayden Daniels, another young star QB. Despite being one of the oldest starting WRs in the league, Diggs was quietly very productive with 85 receptions and over 1,000 yards on a league-leading 85% catch rate. His per-route metrics (2.53 YPRR) behind-the-scenes also suggest he is not quite done. He forms a solid old man receiving duo with Terry McLaurin and should step right into a 20+ % target share on a Commanders team desperate for pass-catchers. Consider Diggs a discounted FLEX option at your drafts on an offense that could be in a ton of shootouts.

Dell missed the entire 2025 season with a catastrophic multi-ligament knee injury, and his timeline for 2026 is still unclear. It looks like he will be able to play some snaps for Houston at some point this year, but he's beginning the regular season on IR as he ramps up. As a result, he should not be on your redraft radar at this time, especially after the team traded for Kayshon Boutte in late August.
current_alert_summary: Placed on IR (designation to return) around Aug 30, 2026; GM Nick Caserio said he's 'close' but 'not quite there' for game action recovering from his Dec 2024 multi-ligament knee injury (missed all of 2025). Will miss at least Houston's first 4 games.

udk_analysis: Tampa took Hurst in the third round of the NFL Draft as he was one of the biggest risers throughout the pre-draft process. Keep expectations in check for Year 1, however. Even though Mike Evans is gone, Egbuka and Godwin are still here, and Jalen McMillan has been productive whenever he has been healthy. Throw in the fact that the Bucs brought in one of the league’s top pass-catching backs in Kenny Gainwell, and it is really tough to see many targets in Year 1 for Hurst. Know the name just in case someone in the Bucs’ WR room gets banged up this year.

Blurb- “Meat Higgins,” as he is known around Fantasy Footballers HQ, has now finished as a top-24 fantasy WR in four of the last five years as the Robin to Ja’Marr Chase’s Batman. As long as Joe Burrow stays healthy, we expect both guys to eat this year, with Higgins the more volatile option of the two Cincy WRs. We are fine with Higgins as a pick where he goes as a WR2 for your squad, but he has always got that sneaky WR1 upside if Chase happens to miss time.
current_alert_summary: Dealing with a heel contusion as of Sept 1, 2026; not considered a major concern for the Sept 13 opener vs Tampa Bay.

udk_analysis: After being one of the most valuable WRs in fantasy in 2024, Scary Terry’s 2025 was a year to forget. Not only did McLaurin deal with injury throughout the season, but the Commanders also lost Jayden Daniels for a significant chunk of the year. To no one’s surprise, the Commanders’ offense was stuck in the mud in what was essentially a lost season. Now, looking forward to 2026, McLaurin has a chance to bounce back in a big way. The depth chart here behind McLaurin is barren, so it wouldn’t be surprising at all to see Terry push for a healthy target share and 8-10 TDs if things break right. McMillan delivered on the promise of being a top-10 NFL Draft pick a year ago, finishing with just over 1,000 yards and seven scores. The draft capital, Year 1 production, and efficiency marks suggest McMillan is poised for another step forward in his sophomore campaign. After seeing 25.4% of the target share a year ago as a rookie, T Mac is on our short list of WRs who could push for upwards of a 30% market share. With his talent, that should mean great things for fantasy.

Tiny Tez! This guy flashed when his number was called in 2025, as Mike Evans and Chris Godwin missed a bunch of time last season. Unfortunately, unless you are an outlier, former seventh-round picks who weigh 165 pounds don’t usually go on to be fantasy stars. Tampa probably views him as a depth piece behind Egbuka, Godwin, McMillan, and Ted Hurst.

Horton got some buzz in camp last summer but ultimately missed the majority of the season because of a shin injury. After the team traded for Rashid Shaheed and then signed him to a new deal in free agency, Horton is just a part- time role player for the Super Bowl champs.

Just as we were starting to see what the man could do last year, he injured his LCL and was out for the season. The WR room is now quite crowded in Jacksonville, and you still aren’t even sure that Hunter will be out there as one. High ceiling, sure, but your basement is literally a sub-level crawl space.

The second-round pick appeared in all 17 games as a rookie but saw just a 7% target share as an afterthought in the offense. In fact, Harris failed to finish inside the top-36 WRs in a single week. His value to the Chargers might be more important to real-life football than fantasy, as this team has multiple other options commanding targets ahead of him. If Ladd McConkey or Quentin Johnston were to miss time, we would be interested in adding Harris as a speculative waiver wire add.

Is there anyone in the NFL with better cardio than Tucker? After running nearly 600 routes in 2024 (fifth most in the NFL), he followed that up with the seventh most among WRs in 2025. He had a monster Week 3 game (8/145/3) against Washington, but then faded back into oblivion, surpassing ten fantasy points just one other time the rest of the season. This Raiders WR room might be one of the worst in the league, giving him yet another year to end up on the field more than you realize. For the game we play, he likely is waiver wire fodder yet again.

You know what’s crazy? There is a world that exists where Treylon Burks is the WR2 for the Commanders in 2026. There are rumors of a Brandon Aiyuk trade or a Stefon Diggs signing, but right now, behind Terry, it is a completely barren depth chart. You don’t need to draft him, but he is worth monitoring in training camp if you play in a deep league.

Heyyyyy, it’s Franklin. If just that drop is all we ever get from Franklin in this silly game we play, we will take it. Unfortunately, that might be the case after the Broncos took Pat Bryant on Day 2 last year, then traded for Jaylen Waddle this offseason. We expect him to be part of Sean Payton’s never-ending WR committee. Aside from injuries to Sutton and Waddle, we can’t recommend putting our beloved Troy into your fantasy lineup at this time.

After spending five years with the Rams as a field-stretching, once-in-a-blue-moon threat, Atwell signed a one-year deal with Miami, joining possibly the worst-looking WR room in the known universe. Opportunity might present itself, but My Guy Sleeper Breakout Value Rookie Bust Injury Concerns Colety Crusaders Redraft Rankings 9/2/2026 remember that Atwell is averaging 1.6 receptions per game in his career. He is unlikely to be a fantasy threat in any way in 2026.
current_alert_summary: Part of the Aug 27-28, 2026 trade sending him back to his original team in exchange for Jarquez Hunter; low standalone fantasy value as a depth WR.

udk_analysis: Tyquan can fill a role for the Chiefs as a situational deep threat, but we cannot imagine a world where he is a consistent starter in your lineup.

Brian Daboll is now in Tennessee, which is potentially very important for Wan’Dale’s fantasy outlook. The two were together in New York over the last few seasons, and we have seen Robinson heavily involved in Daboll’s offense, seeing 140 targets in back-to-back seasons. Carnell Tate has room to grow into the alpha, but Robinson leading the team in targets is definitely in the range of potential outcomes.

We all assumed last year’s rookies (Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel) would steal playing time from boring vets like Xavier Hutchinson, but he was able to keep his role all season, playing 58% of the snaps. Unfortunately, he is not an efficient player and has averaged less than 13 receiving yards per game in his career (hey, don’t laugh!). After Jayden Higgins tore his ACL in camp, Hutchinson could mix in for snaps again this season, but that does not mean he will be fantasy-viable, especially after the team traded for Kayshon Boutte.

Legette lost his WR2 job last year to Jalen Coker, and we are projecting that to stick in 2026. Tetairoa McMillan should dominate the target share here, and Coker is a fine WR2 option for the team. Call us crazy, but we are not drafting Bryce Young’s WR3, especially after he saw four or fewer targets in eight of his final 10 games to close 2025.

Worthy had a chance in 2025 to really take a step forward to start the season while Rashee Rice was serving his suspension. Unfortunately, in the first quarter of the first game of the season, Worthy dislocated his shoulder and never looked right, playing through injury all season. You can certainly explain away some of the down production last year, but truth be told, we still do not know how good a player he is in the league. In two seasons, he is averaging 1.40 yards per route run and earning targets on 18% of his routes. As the kids say, those numbers are pretty mid. Still, we are always interested in taking shots on Mahomes’ pass catchers, and the Chiefs didn’t add any meaningful talent to the WR room this offseason. Entering the season, he is a boom-bust FLEX option.

We know Drake London is the dude here in Atlanta, but behind him, this depth chart is wide open. The Falcons used the 79th overall pick on the former Georgia Bulldog, so he has a realistic opportunity to see the field as a rookie. Electric in the return game and dangerous with the ball in his hands, Branch was used primarily in the screen game and on manufactured touches in college. He is going to have to develop in the NFL to be a factor for fantasy, but perhaps he can be a late-season riser.

With Mr. LOVEland, Luther Burden, and Rome Odunze atop the pecking order, Thomas isn’t on the radar for redraft leagues. Expect him to be a part-time player and contribute on special teams. He did log 40 carries in college and had 95 combined kickoff and punt returns, so he brings some versatility to Chicago, but this is not a guy you need to worry about in your redraft league.

Flowers is coming off a highly efficient 2025 campaign, setting a career high in targets (118), receptions (86), and yards (1,211). Over the last two seasons, Zay has averaged 2.61 and 2.35 yards per route run. Those are some elite marks. The guy is good! Unfortunately, the one bug-a-boo for Zay in fantasy land has been TDs. Through three seasons, he has topped out at just five scores. In order to make the leap into being a real difference maker, he is going to need to find the painted box more often. Perhaps he can fall into an outlier TD year, but with Lamar stealing some attempts in the red zone and King Henry still here, that seems somewhat unlikely for 2026.
current_alert_summary: Held out of some practice 'for precautionary reasons'; expected back to full practice and cleared for Week 1 vs Indianapolis.
